data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism asserts that each straight cut through the center 'corresponds to a diameter' and divides the disk into 2n sectors, but it never establishes the causal step for why the k-th cut, passing through the already-shared center point, splits only two existing regions rather than creating additional intersections. The sector-counting result (2n = 8) is presented as a structural analogy rather than as a line-by-line causal derivation of how concurrency suppresses the extra crossings that would otherwise produce more pieces.
